author: reek
body: The first DHCP exchange this tree has ever performed. Dhcp.codex built messages and parsed replies for its whole life without one of them reaching a wire, so every field asserted below is a field that had never been carried by an actual datagram.

author: reek
body: THE ADDRESS IS NOT WRITTEN OUT HERE AS A COMPARAND. It is printed, and the emulator's NAT is the authority on what it offers; a test that declared 10.0.2.15 and compared against it would pass on a stack that never asked. What makes this able to fail is the state row: an acquisition that gets no answer prints UNCONFIGURED with 0.0.0.0, which is what every run before the server existed did.
